script:
Hello, this is The Portfolio Podcast for SOXX. Friday — here is your SOXX recap. The portfolio closed one point two nine percent up on the session. A strong finish to the week, with most holdings in the green and one notable outlier pulling in the opposite direction.

Citi just slashed its price target on Micron Technology, warning that the memory cycle is starting to turn. The stock fell on the news — and Michael Burry is already short. That tension is worth watching closely.

No broad macro data was available for Friday's session. Markets moved largely on earnings momentum and sector rotation within technology. The Nasdaq posted meaningful gains on the day, led by strength across the semiconductor complex, which provided the primary tailwind for this portfolio.

The dominant story Friday was Micron Technology, and it carries weight for this portfolio. Citi revised its price target downward, citing early signs of a cooling memory market. The framing was pointed — strong profits remain in the near term, but the analyst flagged a cyclical shift beginning to take hold. Separately, SK Hynix announced a thirty-eight billion dollar commitment to new chip manufacturing facilities, aimed at scaling high-bandwidth memory and DRAM production to meet persistent artificial intelligence supply shortages. That kind of capital commitment from a direct competitor adds context to the cycle concern Citi raised. Meanwhile, Michael Burry's short position against Micron, part of a broader semiconductor bearish book, has been building. His pattern, as reported, is to find structural vulnerabilities beneath narratives the market treats as infallible. The combination of an analyst downgrade, a competitor's aggressive expansion, and a high-profile short position makes Micron the most watched name in this portfolio heading into next week.

Advanced Micro Devices was down one point two one percent on the session — the only primary holding in the red on Friday. On its most recent earnings call, analysts pressed hard on whether the company can sustain its growth forecasts without margin compression as it scales. The tension between top-line acceleration and cost structure is the story to watch. Separately, Dell's emerging alliances with Advanced Micro Devices, Nvidia, and Microsoft were cited as a demand signal for the broader ecosystem.

Micron Technology was down zero point four four percent. As covered in depth, the Citi revision and the Burry short are the two threads to follow heading into next week.

Turning to NVIDIA Corporation, up two point two seven percent on Friday. Jim Cramer reiterated his long-term conviction in the name, citing persistent artificial intelligence infrastructure demand. The stock's move higher was one of the stronger individual performers in the semiconductor space on the session.

Broadcom Incorporated was up one point seven one percent. No specific catalyst drove the move — the name tracked broader semiconductor strength and continued to benefit from its diversified chip and infrastructure software exposure.

Over at Intel Corporation, up one point eight four percent on Friday. Intel continues its quiet recovery phase. No fresh news drove the move, but relative performance against its peers remained constructive.

Applied Materials was up two point two one percent. The equipment space showed broad strength Friday, and Applied Materials captured that momentum. Upcoming capital expenditure signals from foundry customers remain the key forward variable.

KLA Corporation was up two point five three percent — one of the stronger performers among the primary holdings on the session. Like Applied Materials, KLA benefits directly from any expansion in wafer fabrication capacity globally, and the SK Hynix spending announcement provides a constructive backdrop.

Meanwhile, Marvell Technology was up three point eight nine percent — the top performer in the portfolio on Friday. No single headline drove the move, but Marvell has strong exposure to custom artificial intelligence silicon and data center interconnect demand, both of which remain in structural growth mode.

Lam Research Corporation was up one point eight two percent. Lam tracks closely with equipment spending cycles, and the same tailwinds supporting KLA and Applied Materials were present here. Foundry capacity expansion news remains the most relevant catalyst to monitor.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company closed up zero point four four percent. The name was the quietest mover among the primary holdings on Friday. As the world's leading contract chipmaker, Taiwan Semiconductor remains a direct beneficiary of any sustained artificial intelligence buildout — the SK Hynix expansion announcement reinforces the supply-side pressure that keeps foundry utilization elevated.

Three data points to watch in the next forty-eight hours. First, any follow-through commentary from Citi or competing analysts on the memory cycle thesis — a second voice either confirming or pushing back on the cooling market narrative will set the tone for Micron Technology early next week. Second, watch for any weekend reporting on United States export control policy updates, which carry direct implications for Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company and the broader semiconductor supply chain. Third, monitor any additional details from SK Hynix on its thirty-eight billion dollar expansion timeline — capital commitment specifics will clarify how quickly competitive high-bandwidth memory supply could pressure pricing across the memory complex.

This is The Portfolio Podcast for SOXX. We will be back same time the next business day with tomorrow's news. The memory cycle debate is the thread to pull — how analysts and the market respond to the Citi revision over the weekend will likely define the early tone on Monday.
